platform: darwin arm64 Apple M3 Max; Go 1.27.3
fixture: 1000 sessions, 100 messages each; full SQLite schema, Porter FTS and trigrams; no private transcripts
interpretation: Initial sequential and first two interleaved upsert cases mix changed and unchanged writes; superseded by true-change samples.
Statistics refresh, analyzed input, reader-cache parity, reopening and WAL state were investigated separately; earlier profiles are not interchangeable controls.
The uncached read-only maintenance opener is not equivalent to the cached serving reader; do not attribute its page speed difference to layout.
Normal app start uses identical ordinary opens and truncated WAL in both archives. This models starting the app after the offline CLI ends.
Immediate post-Compact reads retain about 1 microsecond page and 1.3 microsecond FTS cost in matched controls; cause not fully isolated. This remains an experimental limit.
Times are medians of batch means, not operation p95, application request latency or cold-cache I/O.
Storage figures and conversion duration in initial_sequential precede the targeted ANALYZE addition. Do not treat that duration as final conversion timing.
Optional CJK runtime, peak native memory, actual peak disk use and other operating systems are not validated by these runs.

initial_sequential.command: env CGO_ENABLED=1 GOFLAGS=-trimpath GOPROXY=off go test -tags 'fts5 sqlite_dbstat' ./internal/db -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkMessageIndexConsolidation$' -benchtime=1x -count=3
limitations: Synthetic 1000 sessions x 100 messages; CJK extension absent.
Full production schema, Porter FTS and trigram maintained.
Baseline first, consolidated second; warmup 10 reads, 250 timed samples each.
Prepare overhead included in reads, excluded in write timing. Writes one transaction rolled back; query samples are not randomized, paired confidence intervals, or application parity proof.
Peak RSS/WAL/temp/backup disk not instrumented. Conversion space uses conservative preflight rather than measured peak.
